newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa recovering, condition improves.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa recovering, condition improves.

text.p: Mother Teresa, revered as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with India's destitute, was recovering and her condition had improved after she was admitted to hospital on Friday with heart trouble, her doctor said.
"Her recovery is satisfactory and she has improved a lot since last night," Dr Asim Bardhan, the 86-year-old nun's cardiologist told reporters in the evening at Calcutta's Woodlands Nursing Home.
"She is not critical. She had liquid diet today," he said.
Bardhan said the Roman Catholic missionary was conscious and breathing on her own after initially relying on a respirator. The doctor said he was hopeful she would recover.
It was the third time since August that the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun, who won the 1979 Nobel Peace prize, had been admitted to hospital for emergency care.
Mother Teresa's latest heart trouble began at about 11:30 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Thursday, said Bardhan. "Last night it was serious," he said.
She was admitted to the hospital at 2:30 a.m. (2100 GMT Thursday) with acute left ventricular heart failure, the hospital said in a medical bulletin.
"Her irregular heart rate is persisting. At present she is fully conscious and comfortable," it said.
"She is getting treatment for heart failure...A team of doctors is looking after her," Bardhan said.
Mother Teresa's health began to deteriorate in 1989, when she was fitted with a heart pacemaker.
Since then she has spent time in hospital for heart disease, bacterial pneumonia, broken ribs, malaria, and lung problems.
She spent nearly three weeks at Woodlands Nursing Home in late August and early September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.

Two weeks after returning to her Calcutta-based order, she fell off a chair and hit her head. A brain scan revealed a blood clot in her brain but it disappeared and she was later released from the hospital.
Last Saturday, Mother Teresa received honorary American citizenship, one of only five people in U.S. history, in a ceremony led by U.S. Ambassador to India Frank Wisner.
Diminutive and bowed, her head often shrouded in a sari, Mother Teresa has became a symbol of commitment to the destitute and is considered a living saint to her multitude of followers.
She began her life's work in the slums of Calcutta, India's most densely populated city, in 1949 and has won worldwide admiration for her devotion to the poor.
The Marxist state chief of West Bengal visited Mother Teresa in hospital on Friday. "She looks cheerful and she is all right," Jyoti Basu said.
